problems.title: Two radical domain restrictions
problems.question: Find the domain of y=√(5-|x|)-2x/√(2-x).
problems.idea: A denominator square root must be strictly positive.
steps: The first condition gives -5≤x≤5; the second gives x<2.
Their intersection is [-5,2).

problems.title: A trapezoid with an overhanging leg
problems.question: A trapezoid has legs 5,7 cm and bases 4,8 cm. Find its height.
problems.idea: Signed horizontal projections allow an overhang.
steps: Subtract the equations: 16-8x=24, so x=-1.
Then h²=25-1=24. The negative projection simply means one top vertex overhangs the base.

problems.title: Rationalized radicals cancel completely
problems.question: Simplify $[(3\sqrt3-2\sqrt2)/(5+\sqrt6)-1/(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)]\sqrt2/(\sqrt3+\sqrt2)+4/(\sqrt3+\sqrt2)$.
steps: The first fraction simplifies to √3-√2, and the second to √3+√2.
Their difference is -2√2. After multiplying by √2/(√3+√2), the result is -4/(√3+√2).
The final positive term cancels it.

problems.title: A square-root substitution exposes factors
problems.question: Simplify $[8\sqrt a/(\sqrt a+7)-15\sqrt a/(a+14\sqrt a+49)]\div[(8\sqrt a+41)/(a-49)]+(7\sqrt a-49)/(\sqrt a+7)$.
steps: The bracket is t(8t+41)/(t+7)². Dividing gives t(t-7)/(t+7).
The remaining term is 7(t-7)/(t+7).
Their sum is t-7. Retain a≥0,a≠49.

problems.title: Inradius from leg sum and altitude projections
problems.question: In right ABC, the altitude foot D on AB satisfies AD:BD=1:4 and AC+BC=6. Find the inradius.
problems.idea: The leg ratio is the square root of the projection ratio.
steps: Thus AC:BC=1:2, giving legs 2 and 4.
The hypotenuse is 2√5.

problems.title: Coordinates for an altitude foot
problems.question: In right ABC, C=90°,AC=20,BC=15,CD⊥AB and DK⊥BC. Find DK.
problems.idea: Place the legs along coordinate axes.
formulas: Foot on ax+by=c from origin is c(a,b)/(a²+b²).
steps: Set C=(0,0),A=(20,0),B=(0,15). The hypotenuse is 3x+4y=60.
Its perpendicular foot is D=(60/25)(3,4)=(7.2,9.6).
Since BC is the y-axis, DK is the x-coordinate 7.2.

problems.title: Six integer solutions of a radical inequality
problems.question: Find a so √(x-2)≤a has exactly six integer solutions.
steps: To include 2,3,4,5,6,7 require 2+a²≥7.
To exclude 8 require 2+a²<8.
Thus 5≤a²<6 with a≥0.

problems.title: Minimum sum of square areas from fixed wire
problems.question: A 2 m wire makes two squares. Find the minimum sum of their areas.
problems.idea: The square sides have a fixed sum.
steps: The area sum is at least (1/2)²/2=1/8 m².
Equality holds at u=v=1/4 m, giving two equal squares.

problems.title: Recover two tangent-circle radii
problems.question: Circles touch externally at C and a common external tangent touches them at A,B. AC=6,BC=8. Find the radii.
problems.idea: The angle ACB is right; use tangent and chord geometry.
steps: The tangent-segment argument gives ACB=90°, so AB=10.
For the circle at A, the inscribed chord AC and tangent AB give R=6·10/(2·8)=15/4.
For the circle at B, r=8·10/(2·6)=20/3. Their common-tangent check is AB²=4Rr=100.

problems.title: An entire interval of radical solutions
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{x+2-2\sqrt{x+1}}+\sqrt{x+5-4\sqrt{x+1}}=1$.
problems.idea: Both outer radicands are perfect squares after substitution.
steps: The equation is |t-1|+|t-2|=1.
The distance sum to 1 and 2 equals their separation exactly when 1≤t≤2.
Since x=t²-1, this gives 0≤x≤3.
